evidence.claims: Disclaimers are strong and honest: sim-to-sim, every range assumed, monotone model inflates rank correlation, no gripper printed (README:3, 28, 36). Checked: (a) README:10 headline 'Spearman 0.993 ... the ranking of designs transfers': reproduced, but 282 of the 600 designs have nominal J < 0.05 (they pick almost no fruit), so the whole-space correlation mostly separates working from non-working designs; recomputed within the nominal top 10% (60 designs) Spearman is 0.838, top 25% 0.961, top 50% 0.987. The README's own top-10% overlap (85%) and regret (median 0.004) are the more informative numbers, but the headline and the page lead with 0.993: partial. (b) results.txt header / README:38 imply the nominal world is codesign-agri's fruit; it is a different draw (fail). (c) README:37 'a different seed could move it by as much as the gain': over 6 independent CMA-ES seed pairs the robust gain on held-out worlds is +0.010 to +0.023 (mean 0.015, sd 0.006, all positive); for the reported pair the robust optimum wins 20 of 30 held-out worlds, paired t = 3.5. The caution is honest but miscalibrated (the result is firmer than stated). (d) 'designs that win sit at the bounds' confirmed (Fg 8.0/7.98 of UB 8, w 24.98/25.0 of UB 25). Net: numbers backed, the headline statistic oversells what it measures: 2.
evidence.fitness: Job: a co-design researcher deciding whether a nominal-sim optimum is safe to print. The harness (draw_world/build/score, held-out worlds) is reusable and the robust-vs-nominal result is sound and stable across seeds (my 6-seed rerun). But the answer is mostly built in: the model is monotone in force, width and opening (README says so), the shift ranges are invented, and 'optimising the expected objective over scenarios beats the nominal optimum on the scenario mean' is the textbook result of stochastic/robust optimisation. Nearest prior work, none cited except Tobin et al. (2017): Jakobi et al. (1995) and Koos, Mouret and Doncieux (2013, IEEE TEVC) 'The transferability approach: crossing the reality gap in evolutionary robotics' (the same question, with a transfer measure); Beyer and Sendhoff (2007, CMAME) robust optimisation survey and Taguchi robust design; Peng et al. (2018) dynamics randomisation; Muratore et al. (2022) review of randomised-simulation transfer; design-under-uncertainty co-design (e.g. Ha et al. 2017 / Schaff et al. 2019 on joint morphology-control). No strawberry-harvesting gripper data (e.g. Xiong et al. 2020, J. Field Robotics) anchor the ranges. Not new, sound as a sim-to-sim sanity check; well short of the PhD-level programme bar in research/CLAUDE.md: 2.
evidence.domain: Compared against robust design optimisation practice (Beyer and Sendhoff 2007; scenario/sample-average approximation with held-out scenarios) and the repository's own research rule 'Run the numbers; don't stylise them' (research/CLAUDE.md). Correct: train/test scenario split, common random numbers across designs, print-tolerance modelled as manufacturing noise on the design, tail metrics (p5, worst) reported. Departures: rank transfer summarised by a whole-space Spearman dominated by infeasible-in-practice designs; the robust objective is the mean only although the discussion is about the tail (no CVaR or chance constraint tried); both optima sit on the force and width bounds, so the box, not the physics, sets the design; every shift range (bruise scale 0.7-1.2, friction share 0.1-0.6, stem 0.8-1.4, tolerances 0.3/15%/0.4 mm) is a round number with no source and no sweep of its own width beyond the global 'width' knob, contrary to the 'Run the numbers' rule. A practitioner would accept the harness, not the strength of the headline: 2.

verdict: Every number reproduces byte-for-byte (results.txt and results.json, 29.8 s), and an independent re-implementation of the world, print tolerance and Hertz line-contact scoring with a hand-written Spearman reproduces the headline to three decimals: Spearman 0.9934, nominal optimum 0.653 -> 0.567 (p5 0.465, worst 0.425), robust optimum 0.623 -> 0.582 (0.501, 0.459). The robust gain is firmer than the README says (+0.010 to +0.023 over 6 CMA-ES seed pairs, all positive). But the headline statistic oversells the transfer: 282 of 600 designs pick almost no fruit, and among the nominal top 10% the rank correlation is 0.838, not 0.993; the 'nominal world' is not codesign-agri's fruit as labelled; 5 of 6 seeded core mutations survive the tests; every shift range is invented; and the transferability and robust-optimisation literature the question belongs to is not cited. Finished as scoped; below the bar on verification, claims, fitness and domain.
